statement: A BST is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its children. All stored values are distinct. A final line holds x. Print the floor (largest stored value at most x) and the ceil (smallest stored value at least x), separated by a space; print -1 for an answer that does not exist. Walk the search path once: stepping right past a value at most x updates the floor candidate, stepping left past a value at least x updates the ceil candidate, and equality sets both.
constraints: Values and x are positive; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: Among 2 5 7 8 12 14, 5 is the largest value at most 6 and 7 the smallest at least 6.

hint: Two notebook variables, both starting at -1; the walk overwrites them as it turns.
mistake: Stopping the walk when x itself is missing - the candidates collected so far are the whole answer.
